info.name: TryOrder Odoo 19 - Complete HTTP API
info.description:
# TryOrder / Odoo 19 HTTP API

Import this file in Postman. `db` defaults to the staging `bunbastic-stg-39985581` database. Each protected request already sends `X-Api-Key: {{apiKey}}`; the supplied staging test key is included in the Collection variable `apiKey`. Use the SAME key value previously stored in `order_connector.api_key`; configure that value as the TryOrder connection Inbound Secret (`webhook_secret`) in Core. Rotate the staging test key before sharing this collection outside the test team. The header remains `X-Api-Key`; the inbound paths remain `/order_connector/*`.

Configure the TryOrder branch binding and payment mappings. For a legacy POS response, open the mapped POS session and configure automatic acceptance plus an invoice customer. Run Ping, Branches and Catalog first. Catalog suggests `branchId`, `productTemplateId`, `unitPrice`, and an `imageUrl`; verify the selected IDs and prices. The image request is skipped when the catalog has no pictured product.

A successfully created POS order returns the old external response fields: `success`, `order_id` (the `pos.order.id` as a string), `order_name` (Odoo POS name), `state` (Odoo POS state), and `kind=pos`. Use that returned `orderId` in status routes. The status response reports the same ID, current Odoo POS `state`, and the incoming `status`. The provider_order_id in a request is TryOrder's own unique ID, not an Odoo ID. Run Cash create, Exact replay, then Conflicting replay in that order; other create examples generate distinct provider IDs. Run folder 05 in order: it creates separate orders for rejected and canceled. A delivered order cannot transition to either status.

The current Core integration can still return `kind=core` with a Core ID when POS is pending. That is a known difference from the old module, which used a Sale order fallback. Coupon and loyalty discounts use separate untaxed negative POS lines while Core stores their breakdown; wallet remains a payment. The discount may not exceed the order total. Run these examples with a product price greater than the discount amounts. Product image URLs are signed and branch-scoped, unlike the old public-by-ID URLs. The POS-waiting and signed-image differences are intentional and remain documented.

A nonzero delivery fee requires an untaxed fee product on the branch. Wallet is a payment, not a discount. Odoo computes product tax; any supplied `total` must equal product + modifier + tax + fee minus coupon/loyalty discounts. Use `expectedOrderState` only if you know the actual Odoo POS state. POS frontend and Kitchen display need separate visual verification. Requests include `?db={{db}}` and `X-Odoo-Database` for the staging Odoo database. Outbound gateway calls are outside this inbound HTTP collection.

item.name: 01 Connection and catalog

request.description: Validates X-Api-Key against an active connected TryOrder Core connection.
Lists active POS store bindings. IDs are pos.config IDs, not Core store binding IDs.

exec: const simple = data.items.find(function (item) { return item.type !== "combo" && !(item.add_on || []).some(function (a) { return Number(a.modifierCategory && a.modifierCategory.min_selection) > 0; }); });

request.description: Inspect items[].add_on[].modifier._id for posmod-ID and items[].combos[].items[].id for comboitem-ID. Select the correct parent product for each option. The script suggests a basic product and captures a signed image URL.

Run Catalog first. Catalog refreshes imageUrl from a product that actually has an image. This request is skipped when the catalog contains none. A signed URL is valid for a connected TryOrder branch or an opted-in Test Draft branch. The response MIME type must match the stored image.

item.name: 04 Status updates

request.description: Provider confirmed/accepted state. Depending on Core policy, order may already be accepted.
POST and PUT use the same status route. Run this after accepted and before ready on the same order.
Advance the selected order to preparing.
Repeat the preceding preparing update with identical payload. Core should return the same state without a second transition.
Advance the selected order to ready.
Advance the selected order to picked_up.
Maps completed to Core delivered; terminal transition.

item.description: Use orderId from a successful create response. Run accepted, POST preparing, PUT preparing and its replay, ready, picked_up, then completed. Completed is terminal; folder 05 creates separate orders for rejected and canceled.

item.name: 05 Alternative status outcomes

request.description: Creates an independent order for the following terminal status request. Run this first.
Run POST new order for rejection immediately before this request. The status uses its own order ID.
Creates an independent order for the following terminal status request. Run this first.
Run POST new order for cancellation immediately before this request. The status uses its own order ID.

item.description: Each terminal outcome gets a fresh order. Run this folder in order: create for rejection, reject, create for cancellation, cancel. A delivered order must return 409 for either terminal change.

item.name: 06 Validation and authorization errors

request.description: Authentication rejection.
Authenticated connection cannot see an unrelated POS branch. Choose an actually unbound ID.

exec: pm.test("Image rejected with HTTP 404", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(404); });
